BiblicalUsage: Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished, and a poor wise man delivered a city by his wisdom, yet no man remembered him, and his wisdom was despised and his words were not heard. Ecclesiastes keeps returning to the poor wise man, and the world keeps forgetting him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the poor wise man is the preacher's portrait of wisdom itself: it delivers the city and is despised for it, and the world remembers the king who would not listen. The world remembers the king who would not listen, and forgets the poor man who saved the city.
